facts.fact_text: On 18 November 2003 at around 10.50 a.m. a group of twenty-three individuals, including the applicants, entered the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse in Istanbul.
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "End the Isolation" ("Tecride Son").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "No to invasion" ("İşgale Hayır").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Close İmralı Prison" ("İmralı Cezaevi Kapatılsın").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "We have not surrendered and we will not surrender" ("Teslim olmadık olmayacağız").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Salute, salute a thousand salutes to İmralı" ("Selam, Selam, İmralıya Bin Selam").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Freedom to Öcalan" ("Öcalan'a Özgürlük").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "The messenger of peace is in İmralı" ("Barış elçisi İmralı'da").
Subsequently, some members of the group closed the door to the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Some members of the group locked themselves in the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse by toppling metal cupboards behind the door.
Members of the group hung a large banner from one of the windows of the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Members of the group threw leaflets outside from the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Witnesses mainly reported hearing repetitive slogans being chanted outside in the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Witnesses reported that they had come to no harm during the protest.
The incident report of 18 November 2003 drawn up by the Deputy Public Prosecutor of Istanbul indicated that no material damage had been caused in the corridor or to its furniture.
The protesters, including the applicants, continued their actions for about an hour until the police broke in and arrested them.
The protesters, including the applicants, continued their actions for about an hour until the police broke in and arrested them.
According to the Government's version of events, the protesters resisted the police officers during their arrest by locking arms.
According to the Government's version of events, the police used tear gas to disperse the protesters because the protesters had resisted by locking arms.
The applicants contested the Government's version of events, arguing that they had surrendered to the police but that they had nevertheless been beaten at the time of their arrest.
Following their arrest, the applicants were first taken to Haseki Hospital.
Following their arrest, the applicants were examined by the Forensic Medicine Institute.

According to the medical reports added to the case file, all of the applicants, except for Mehmet Şahin, Özgür Tan and Mahmut Cengiz, presented signs of physical trauma, either at the beginning or at the end of their custody.
The medical reports drawn up in respect of the applicant Ekrem Can at the beginning of his time in police custody did not note any signs of ill-treatment.
The medical reports drawn up in respect of the applicant Fikret Avras at the beginning of his time in police custody did not note any signs of ill-treatment.
The medical reports compiled at the end of the applicant Ekrem Can's time in police custody concluded that he had been unfit for work for a period of one day.
The medical reports compiled at the end of the applicant Fikret Avras's time in police custody concluded that he had been unfit for work for a period of one day.
Between 18 and 22 November 2003, the applicants were held in police custody on terrorism-related charges.
Between 18 and 22 November 2003, the applicants were interviewed by the Anti-Terrorism branch of the Istanbul Security Directorate.
According to some documents in the case file, most of the applicants met their lawyer before giving statements to the police.
According to some documents in the case file, most of the applicants met their lawyer after giving statements to the police.
According to forms bearing the signature of each applicant (save for the applicant Mehmet Şahin), the applicants chose to give their statements without the presence of a lawyer.
The forms bearing the applicants' signatures indicated that each applicant had been informed of his rights under Article 135 of the former Code of Criminal Procedure.
The forms bearing the applicants' signatures indicated that a copy of a form explaining their rights had been handed to each applicant.
The forms bearing the applicants' signatures did not bear the time at which they had been signed, but the dates were recorded by hand.
The applicant Mehmet Şahin was the only applicant who requested the assistance of a lawyer during the taking of his statement by the police.
A certain A.P., who is not one of the applicants, also appears to have requested the assistance of a lawyer during the taking of his statement by the police.
The applicant Mehmet Şahin was interviewed in the presence of a lawyer and remained silent before the police.
A.P. was interviewed in the presence of a lawyer and remained silent before the police.
The officers involved in the questioning of the applicant Mehmet Şahin and A.P. were not the same as those involved in the questioning of the other applicants.
The applicant Kerim Taştan exercised his right to remain silent without requesting the assistance of a lawyer.
The rest of the applicants (other than Mehmet Şahin, A.P. and Kerim Taştan) gave statements to the police between 19 and 21 November 2003, in the absence of a lawyer.

The statements of the applicants were transcribed on printed forms, the first page of which indicated inter alia that they were suspected of acting on behalf of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), an illegal organisation.

The first page of the printed forms used for the applicants' statements included a printed message stating inter alia that the person being questioned had the right to remain silent and the right to choose a lawyer.
On each of the applicants' forms, the box entitled "No lawyer sought" was marked with a printed "X", indicating that all the applicants refused legal assistance.
According to the police statement records, all the applicants except for one also stated that they did not wish to have a lawyer or to remain silent.
The applicant Fikret Avras met a lawyer on 19 November 2003 at 10.35 a.m.
The applicant Fikret Avras met a different lawyer on 21 November 2003 at 9.30 p.m.
The applicant Ekrem Can met a lawyer on 19 November 2003 at 11.20 a.m.

The applicants, except for Kerim Taştan and Mehmet Şahin (who did not give statements to the police), acknowledged having wilfully participated in the protest at the Sultanahmet Courthouse on 18 November 2003, pursuant to decisions made by the council of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan).
Many of the applicants acknowledged having taken part in other protests organised in support of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan).
On 21 November 2003 the applicants Ekrem Can and Fikret Avras participated in an identity parade conducted with photographs (fotoğraftan teşhis).
The applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz were taken to certain locations for a reconstruction of the events in question (yer gösterme) on 21 November 2003.
During the reconstruction of events (yer gösterme), the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz were not assisted by a lawyer.

During the reconstruction of events (yer gösterme), the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz acknowledged having been involved in throwing Molotov cocktails at police vehicles on different occasions.

During the reconstruction of events (yer gösterme), the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz acknowledged having been involved in throwing stones at public buses on different occasions.
During the reconstruction of events (yer gösterme), the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz acknowledged having been involved in attacking a bank on different occasions.

The applicant Fikret Avras gave a similar version of events to that of Mahmut Cengiz at the hearing on 19 April 2004.
